title: Market sell-off, tax scrutiny and growth: key figures shaping investor sentiment
text:
Market sell-off, tax scrutiny and growth: key figures shaping investor sentiment | South China Morning Post Markets - Markets Market sell-off, tax scrutiny and growth: key figures shaping investor sentiment Advertisement Hong Kong stock market Business Markets Market sell-off, tax scrutiny and growth: key figures shaping investor sentiment 
 A stock market slump, Beijing’s tax enforcement drive and fresh GDP data are among the developments drawing investors’ attention this week
 2 -MIN READ 2 -MIN Listen Christina Zhao Published: 3:00pm, 23 Oct 2026 As regional equities tumbled and hopes for investor stimulus faded, the Hang Seng Index fell to a seven-month low. Attention also remained focused on Beijing’s intensified scrutiny of offshore wealth and tax compliance . Macroeconomic data pointed to steady, if uneven, domestic momentum. Here are the core figures capturing market attention this week.
 Hong Kong stocks suffer steepest drop in 7 months 
 The Hang Seng Index sank 3.03 per cent in a single session to 22,934.68 points, its worst performance since March, as slowing profit growth among major tech firms and reduced expectations for stimulus weighed on sentiment.
 Investors were also concerned about potential share sales ahead of Beijing’s Thursday deadline for offshore trust gains. Shares of Chinese toymaker Bloks Group plunged after its chairman sold a 1.6 per cent stake for HK$250 million (US$31.9 million), a move that some market watchers linked to liquidity needs arising from the new tax regime.
 China’s tax workforce recruitment drive accelerates 
 China’s 2027 national civil service recruitment plan includes 24,013 tax-related positions, accounting for more than 67 per cent of all vacancies, up from over 65 per cent a year earlier.
